summary: The agent passed all 46 new tests. The recorded baseline failure is a verifier-generated missing-test error after an existing concurrency test was legitimately parameterized; both replacement cases passed, as did every other executed graded test.

details.reasoning: junit_new.xml records 46 tests with zero failures, errors, or skips. junit_base.xml records 41/42 expected baseline IDs passing, but its only failure says 'base tests were missing from the JUnit XML (exit code 0).' This is not an application assertion failure. The agent expanded TextFileBasedViolationStoreConcurrencyTest.is_safe_when_multiple_instances_save_to_the_same_store_concurrently() into a parameterized test taking String integrity, with values ignore and repair. It retained the concurrency workload and assertions. wrapper_output.xml contains both corresponding '(String) [1]' and '(String) [2]' cases as passing, and all three actual baseline suites have zero failures and errors: 43 executed baseline invocations passed. The wrapper's add_missing_failures function nevertheless inserts a base-fallback failure for the obsolete no-argument name. All 89 actually executed graded test cases passed; the 90th case is synthetic. The implementation genuinely adds disk-state reloads, broken/resolved-entry repair, shared-file identity checks, and empty-save forgetting behavior. The test edits add coverage rather than weaken it; restoring the original concurrency test would restore the expected ID, not expose a demonstrated implementation failure. No causal cheating was found. FAIL_TEST_BROKEN is therefore more appropriate than FAIL_REGRESSION or an agent-fault verdict.
details.secondary_factors: The solve-time trajectory also contains real, recovered build-environment friction. Calls 23-25 investigate a missing compiled TextFileBasedViolationStore$RuleViolationFileNameStrategy class despite its unchanged interface remaining in source, then use a clean build to recover. The hidden test.sh independently documents that the shared jdk9main output can prune incremental-build classes. Call 26 reports an uncached google-java-format:1.30.0 dependency; subsequent resolution/debugging culminates in a proxy HTTP 403 in call 34 and termination of the blocked formatter process in call 35. These inspections, clean-rebuild workaround, and formatter-resolution attempts would be unnecessary in a healthy build image. They did not prevent eventual test validation: calls 38-39 record a successful clean core build with 15,857 tests and zero failures/errors. These are secondary environment issues, not the cause of the synthetic grading failure.

quick_failure_summary: Baseline grading rejects an obsolete test ID despite both equivalent parameterized replacements passing.

justification.issue_description: The verifier matches a fixed no-argument baseline JUnit name and incorrectly synthesizes a failure when the same test is expanded into passing ignore/repair parameterized invocations.
justification.evidence: The task describes store integrity behavior and does not require preserving JUnit method signatures or display names. agent_solution.patch changes @Test to @ParameterizedTest with @ValueSource(strings = {"ignore", "repair"}) and adds the integrity property, without removing the original concurrency assertions. wrapper_output.xml:37 and wrapper_output.xml:38 show the '(String) [1]' and '(String) [2]' cases passing. junit_base.xml:43 instead contains a synthetic failure for the original 'is_safe_when_multiple_instances_save_to_the_same_store_concurrently()' name. wrapper_addendum.patch's add_missing_failures function generates that failure from the fixed expected-node-ID manifest; this identity constraint is wrapper bookkeeping, not a behavioral requirement in test.patch or the visible task.
justification.verdict_reasoning: A competent developer could reasonably parameterize an existing regression test to cover both integrity modes while preserving its assertions. The recorded failure does not establish broken functionality, an undocumented output convention, or a missing integrity requirement: it is an erroneous baseline-identity comparison. The primary fault lies in the verifier's inability to recognize the passing replacement cases, so FAIL_TEST_BROKEN is the appropriate verdict.

problem_assessment.notes: The core task is challenging but solvable and reasonably explicit about initialization freshness, invalid paths, shared names/file identities, symbolic and hard links, and deletion failure ordering. The reference solution demonstrates feasibility, and the new tests exercise the specified behaviors without a demonstrated requirement mismatch. The grading infrastructure is not fair to a benign test parameterization: restore baseline tests independently for grading or verify equivalent parameterized coverage before declaring a stored node ID missing. Also make incremental compilation reliable and pre-cache the configured formatter for the offline environment.
